name: Beyond The Ego
body:
School enchantment [mind-affecting, void]; Level psychic 6, shaman 6, sorcerer/wizard 6

Casting Time 2 rounds

Components V, S, DF

Range medium (100 ft. + 10 ft./level)

Target one intelligent creature

Duration concentration

Saving Throw see text; Spell Resistance yes

Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

You target an intelligent (Int 3 or higher) creature’s mind and forcefully connect them to the Void, bombarding their awareness with cosmic enlightenment. This dissolves the boundaries between their ego and the observable world, leading to a state of spiritual tranquility of oneness and nothingness.

While you maintain concentration on this spell, the target gains the paralyzed condition, unable to take even mental actions. There is no initial saving throw to resist the spell from taking effect but each round at the start of their turn, the target may attempt a Will save to end the spell. A target can expend 1 ki point as an immediate action to gain an initial Will save to prevent the spell from taking effect on them.

While this spell lasts, if the target suffers any damage, affliction, or penalty, they gain a Will save immediately to end this spell.

When the spell ends, the target does not retain any memory or comprehension of the glimpsed truths and insights imparted by the Void in this way but they may have a momentary sense of loss or déjà vu.
